title: Wok-Steamed Broccoli with Ginger-Sesame Sauce
description: Fresh broccoli steams just to crisp-tender and picks up a glossy ginger sauce with a little toasted sesame oil.

ingredients.name: fresh broccoli florets
ingredients.note: Use bite-size 1-inch florets, splitting thick stems lengthwise.

steps.title: Whisk the sauce
steps.text: Whisk {broth}, {ginger}, {aminos} and {starch} together in a bowl until the starch disperses.

steps.title: Steam the broccoli
steps.text: Bring {water} to a boil in the HexClad wok. Add {broccoli}, cover, and steam for 3–5 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender at the stem.

steps.title: Lift out the florets
steps.text: Transfer the broccoli to a warm bowl with a slotted spoon and pour off any remaining steaming water.

steps.title: Thicken the ginger sauce
steps.text: Whisk the sauce mixture again, pour it into the wok, and simmer over medium heat for 1 minute until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Coat the florets
steps.text: Turn off the heat and fold the broccoli and {oil} into the sauce. Serve immediately while the stems retain their bite.

notes: Make ahead: Cut the florets and whisk the sauce base up to a day ahead. Store separately and stir the sauce well before cooking. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Frozen and reheated florets lose their crisp-tender texture. Fridge reheat: Warm covered in the wok with a splash of water for 3–5 minutes, folding once, until the center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge reheat instructions. Option A uses the measured ginger juice. Option B omits the ginger for a milder sesame sauce. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 80 kcal, 3.6 g protein, 11.5 g total carbohydrate, 2.1 g fat, 3.1 g fiber, 118 mg sodium.

steps.title: Set up the cooking vessel
steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
